name: Hemp Rope
description: Twenty paces of Vale hemp, tarred at the ends. The Merrowby rope-walk marks every coil with a red thread so a borrowed rope can be sent home.

name: Lantern Oil
description: Pressed from rape and eel, which is why every lantern in Wickmere smells faintly of the marsh.

name: Tallow Candle
description: A plain candle. On Candle Night every window in the Vale burns one, and the Dwindling is said to step back a pace.

name: Pitch Torch
description: Burns an hour. Deep places dislike it; so do sneaks.

name: Lockpick
description: A sliver of sprung steel. Sold openly in Tollmere, quietly in Merrowby, and not at all in Kharrow Hold, where a lock is a host's word.

name: Sack of Flour
description: Larkbourne barley, ground at a mill that still has a miller. Bread prices follow this sack.

name: Sealed Parcel
description: Waxed cloth, string, a name in charcoal. Somebody is waiting for it, which in Wickmere is nearly the same as somebody remembering you.

name: Waxed Cloth
description: Keeps rain off parcels and powder. Reedfolk dye theirs indigo; Vale folk leave it the colour of old butter.

name: Charcoal
description: Burnt slow in a Briarwold clamp by people who do not talk much. Smiths buy it by the sack.

name: Iron Ingot
description: Skerrow bog-iron, smelted in Brindlecrag and carried down the chain roads. Stamped with a clan mark that means 'remembered'.

name: Iron Nails
description: A handful. A house is mostly nails and talk.

name: Whetstone
description: Grey Skerrow stone. Ten strokes a side, the smiths say, and think of the person you will meet.

name: Iron Knife
description: A kitchen blade that has been to more barrows than kitchens. Quick, quiet, and sixfold cruel to a back that does not know you are there.

name: Hand Axe
description: Splits kindling and, when it must, the argument. Every Vale house has one by the door.

name: Leather Jerkin
description: Boiled and waxed. It will not stop a Hart-Knight, but it will stop a hedge from stopping you.

name: Iron Cap
description: A plain skullcap with a nasal. Wardens wear theirs pushed back so children can see their faces.

name: Watercress
description: From the Larkbourne shallows below Merrowby. Peppery. The herbwives say it clears the blood and the temper.

name: Marsh Marigold
description: Gold in the teal. Reedfolk float one on a burial lantern; alchemists float one in a healing draught.

name: Ember Salt
description: Scraped from a hearth that has never gone out. Warm to the touch for a year. Sayers pay too much for it.

name: Bitterleaf
description: Young bracken, dried. Bitter as the name and as honest.

name: Empty Phial
description: Tollmere glass, thin and greenish. Holds one draught or a great deal of hope.

name: Healing Draught
description: Watercress, marigold and a pinch of ember salt. Tastes of pond and comfort.

name: Barley Loaf
description: Dense, dark, still warm if you are lucky. The price tells you whether the miller is alive.

name: Apple Pie
description: The only apples in Wickmere grow in Hearthvale, so this is the only pie. Bring one and be forgiven.

name: Tamwick Cider
description: From the only press. Cloudy, sharp, and the reason Long Table lasts until morning.

name: Eel Stew
description: Lake-eel, barley and whatever the cook was thinking about. Better in Gullhithe; more honest in Isseva.

name: Lake Eel
description: Slick, grey, still moving a little. Brightwater's staple and Sedgemire's poetry.

name: Smoked Eel
description: Hung on the Gullhithe racks until it is more smoke than eel. Keeps for a season; tastes of the shore.

name: Fish Hooks
description: Bone in the marsh, iron on the lake. Either will hold an eel that wants holding.

name: Reed Net
description: Knotted by someone singing a round. The knots are the verses; you can hear it if you know the song.
